statement: In mixed-size scenes with moderate or high diameter dispersion, the declared median/90th-percentile two-tier hash emits fewer unique broad-phase candidate pairs than the best single-tier hash on the predeclared cell-size grid.
measurable_prediction: For each identical scene, paired_difference = two_tier_unique_candidates - minimum_single_tier_unique_candidates will be below zero in the specified mixed-size regimes; summarize the per-condition median and range across seeds.
regime: Lognormal medium/high dispersion, separated bimodal mixtures, and Pareto-like sizes; uniform and clustered centers; sparse and crowded density levels.
falsifier: The paired difference is nonnegative for every replicated condition in these regimes, or any apparent reduction disappears when all methods use the same de-duplication and boundary rules.

statement: There is a low-dispersion crossover at which the two-tier policy loses its candidate-count advantage because both tiers approximate the same useful spatial scale and the extra tier creates duplicate or poorly filtered visits.
measurable_prediction: As size dispersion increases from mono-size/low-dispersion controls, the paired difference changes from nonnegative to negative under a predeclared sign-change rule, or remains nonnegative if no crossover is observed.
regime: Mono-size and low-dispersion lognormal scenes, followed by the first adjacent medium-dispersion condition, with density held fixed.
falsifier: No sign change occurs across the declared dispersion sequence, or the observed sign is not consistent across the minimum required seed set.

statement: A two-mode size distribution with modes separated beyond the single-cell resolution range is the regime most likely to benefit from two scales derived from the median and 90th percentile.
measurable_prediction: The separated-bimodal condition has a more negative two-tier-versus-oracle paired difference than the mono-size and low-dispersion controls at matched object count, domain, and density.
regime: Bimodal mixtures with explicitly recorded mode ratio and separation; compare against a same-mean or same-median unimodal control.
falsifier: The bimodal effect is absent, smaller than the matched controls, or cannot be reproduced from the same scene files.

statement: For a heavy-tailed size distribution, median and 90th-percentile scales may not cover the extreme tail well enough to beat the best single tier, so the adaptive policy has a null or negative result despite high dispersion.
measurable_prediction: The Pareto-like condition has a nonnegative paired difference, or a weaker reduction than the separated-bimodal condition, after truncation and realized quantiles are reported.
regime: Truncated Pareto-like diameters with a small extreme-object fraction and otherwise matched domain, count, and center distribution.
falsifier: A robust reduction at least as large as the separated-bimodal effect is reproduced across seeds and remains after reporting the number of cells traversed by extreme objects.

statement: Any candidate-count benefit of the two-tier policy depends on occupancy: crowded or clustered scenes can amplify scale mismatch, while very sparse scenes can make both methods nearly equivalent.
measurable_prediction: At matched size distribution, the absolute and relative paired differences differ between sparse uniform, crowded uniform, and clustered conditions, with the largest magnitude in at least one crowded or clustered regime.
regime: Uniform and clustered centers crossed with declared sparse and crowded occupancy controls.
falsifier: Paired differences are indistinguishable across density/spatial-distribution levels, or the apparent interaction is explained by unequal realized overlap counts or regenerated scenes.

statement: For mono-size objects, a two-tier median/90th-percentile hash does not systematically reduce candidate pairs relative to the best single-tier grid because both derived scales coincide up to the percentile convention.
measurable_prediction: The mono-size paired difference is zero or nonnegative for nearly all seeds, with any deviation attributable to explicit tie-breaking, boundary, or assignment policy rather than size adaptation.
regime: Deterministic mono-size AABB controls at sparse and crowded densities.
falsifier: A negative reduction persists across seeds under identical scales, identical pair de-duplication, and an independently checked single-tier implementation.

statement: The tier assignment/query policy is a material determinant of candidate count; changing only whether objects are inserted into one selected tier or both tiers can reverse the apparent benefit attributed to the median/90th-percentile statistics.
measurable_prediction: At least one mixed-size condition shows a different sign or materially different magnitude of paired difference between the primary policy and the declared sensitivity policy.
regime: A representative separated-bimodal and heavy-tail scene set, with scales fixed from the same realized diameter statistics.
falsifier: All assignment/query policies produce indistinguishable candidate counts, or the comparison changes scales, scene generation, or de-duplication in addition to policy.

statement: Diameter-based tiers are less effective for strongly anisotropic AABBs than for near-cubic AABBs because one scalar diameter does not capture the number of cells spanned along each axis.
measurable_prediction: For matched diameter distributions, anisotropic objects show a smaller or nonnegative two-tier reduction and a larger cells-per-object or duplicate-emission burden than near-cubic objects.
regime: Near-cubic control versus declared anisotropic aspect-ratio condition, with identical centers, diameters, counts, and density settings.
falsifier: Anisotropic scenes show the same or greater replicated reduction without a corresponding difference in cell span or duplicate workload.

statement: After global unordered-pair de-duplication, candidate counts are invariant to object insertion order and object-ID permutation; any order dependence indicates an implementation confound rather than an algorithmic effect.
measurable_prediction: Permuting IDs and insertion/query order leaves each method's unique candidate count unchanged for the same scene, while raw emission counts may vary only before de-duplication.
regime: At least one deterministic mixed-size fixture and one clustered fixture, run with declared permutations.
falsifier: Unique candidate counts change under permutation, or the implementation cannot distinguish raw emissions from deduplicated candidate pairs.

statement: A lower candidate count, if observed, will not necessarily imply a lower false-positive ratio or lower computational cost; candidate reduction must be reported separately from true AABB overlaps, insertion/query work, and memory-related measures.
measurable_prediction: For every surviving reduction, at least one condition can be identified where candidate count and candidate/true-overlap ratio do not move in the same direction, or the data explicitly show that no such divergence occurred within the bounded matrix.
regime: All conditions with nonzero true-overlap counts, emphasizing crowded and anisotropic scenes.
falsifier: The analysis claims time, memory, cache, or narrow-phase accuracy from candidate counts alone, or omits undefined ratios and zero-overlap conditions.
